extracted.intended_audience: authors and reviewers of systematic reviews on open peer review; researchers in scholarly communication and open science
extracted.subtask_description: Peer review guidance and reviewer report for a systematic review about Open Peer Review (OPR) and Open Science, focusing on clarity of definitions, methodological transparency, disciplinary coverage (STEM vs SSH), interpretation, and scope. Useful for authors revising and peer reviewers assessing similar systematic reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rationale and objectives clarity
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the rationale for, and objectives of, the Systematic Review clearly stated?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer response: Yes. Ensure the Introduction clearly states the definition of open science used and the paper's aims; unpack contested meanings if the definition is not universally accepted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Methods detail for replication
rubrics_metrics.description: Are sufficient details of the methods and analysis provided to allow replication by others?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer response: Partly. Provide full search strategies (search terms) for all databases and search engines used (not just Web of Science), specify which databases were searched, and clearly describe selection criteria and analysis steps so others can replicate. Expand the methodology section and include a statement regarding limitations of the search strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the statistical analysis and its interpretation appropriate?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer: I cannot comment; a qualified statistician is required. If quantitative methods are used, have a qualified statistician check analyses and interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conclusions supported by results
rubrics_metrics.description: Are the conclusions drawn adequately supported by the results presented in the review?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer response: Partly. Ensure conclusions reflect the limits of the data and methods, explicitly acknowledge disciplinary differences and methodological limitations, and avoid claims that go beyond the review's scope or evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and scoping of Open Science / OPR
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly define and scope 'Open Science' and 'Open Peer Review' (OPR); state the ethos being invoked and whether the definition is contested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommends explicitly stating the definition used in the Introduction, unpacking contested meanings, and making the definition inclusive of social sciences and humanities perspectives. A clear scope strengthens framing and interpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address disciplinary differences (STEM vs SSH)
rubrics_metrics.description: Acknowledge and engage with tensions between STEM and social sciences/humanities approaches to and understandings of peer review and OPR.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggests adding more consideration of SSH perspectives (e.g., Fitzpatrick), including disciplinary breakdowns (figures/tables), and discussing how community-based or mentorship aspects in SSH affect meaning-making and acceptance of OPR.

rubrics_metrics.name: Search strategy and SSH coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Searching for and selection of social sciences and humanities literature should be explicit and adequate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide search terms for each database/search engine used, document database coverage beyond Web of Science, and outline any gaps or limitations in retrieving SSH literature; justify exclusions or scope decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of figures and tables to translate findings
rubrics_metrics.description: Present figures and tables to translate findings and ideas, especially for non-quantitative readers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer notes that figures and tables help translate results; consider adding visual breakdowns of traits by discipline and other summary visuals to aid comprehension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope and out-of-scope clarity (economic arguments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clearly state what is in and out of scope (e.g., whether to address economic arguments such as APCs and their effects).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggests unpacking counterarguments about economic implications (APCs, access for unfunded research) if included, or explicitly note that these broader economic debates fall outside the review's scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish peer review process from platform
rubrics_metrics.description: Clarify the distinction between the peer review process itself and the technological/platform implementations that support it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid techno-determinism; explicitly note that peer review can be decoupled from journals and platforms (add explanatory sentence). Make clear when discussion refers to platforms versus processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Engage with literature on OPR's effects (mentorship, collaboration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider evidence about whether and how OPR changes the role and purpose of peer review (e.g., mentorship at eLife, reviewer engagement at Frontiers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer recommends deeper engagement with literature demonstrating OPR's effects on mentorship, reviewer interaction and robustness of review; if this question is out of scope, state so but acknowledge its importance for future research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Present limitations of the method
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicitly present and discuss the limitations of the review's methods and dataset.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State limitations of the search strategy, disciplinary coverage, inclusion/exclusion criteria, and any analytical constraints; clarifying limitations will help scope conclusions and improve scientific soundness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Organization and readability
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the paper well written, organized logically, and readable?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer: The paper is well written and logically organized, making it readable and easy to follow. Maintain clear organization and readability while adding the recommended clarifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clarify assumed purpose of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Define the assumed purpose(s) of peer review used as the basis for analysis (vetting, fact checking, substantive feedback, mentorship, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer suggests clarifying the purpose of peer review in the Introduction and throughout the paper to support arguments about whether OPR is changing peer review's role; tie this definition to sections (e.g., open final-version commenting).
